contributes.instructions: Pasting HTML on the canvas (Cmd+V with markup as plain text, or text/html that is more than a single paragraph of prose; a paragraph copied from a page lands as canvas text through the Text plugin instead) lands it as one new daydream.viewport item, 960px wide and selected: the fragment's element structure, text, inline style attributes and its class, id and data-* attributes are kept; every style block, in head or body, lands as the viewport's sheet — the flat rules the browser parses, nesting flattened, @media, @container and @supports ancestry as conditions, !important stripped and counted, @font-face lifted into fonts — while @import, @layer, @keyframes and @property are counted and lost; an inline svg is kept as the drawing it is — its subset of shapes, text, gradients, clips, masks, symbols and use, markers and filters, its presentation attributes (fill, stroke, …) lifted into styles, what the subset lacks (image, foreignObject, animation, an external href on a use) dropped and counted; a tag the format cannot hold becomes a span (phrasing content) or a div; every other attribute, linked stylesheets, scripts and embedded content are dropped; a data: image is vendored, an https: image stays, any other image source is dropped with the img kept. No gates run on a paste; the console reports what was lost. A paste of more than 10,000 elements or four million characters is refused and lands nothing; past 64 levels of nesting an element lands as a leaf holding its words.
